# Brainstorm 10 name ideas for a side project with Cohere

> **In short:** Cohere's chat assistant can generate a list of creative name ideas from a short prompt you write in plain English. You'll need a free Cohere account, a web browser, and about five minutes — no coding or paid plan required for basic use.

You've got a side project on the couch cushions, but the name? Nothing. You could stare at a blank page for an hour, or you could spend five minutes bouncing ideas with an AI. Cohere — a chat-based AI assistant from the company Cohere — is built for exactly this kind of quick, text-focused thinking. You type what you want, and it sends back a list of ideas you can mix, match, and edit.

## Before you start
- A free Cohere account (sign up with an email at cohere.com).
- A web browser on a phone, tablet, or computer.
- A rough idea of what your project IS — even one sentence is enough (a podcast about old movies, a candle business, a neighborhood walking club).
- About 5 minutes total.

## Step 1 — Open Cohere and start a new chat
Go to **cohere.com** in your browser and sign in. Once you're in, look for a **"New chat"** button or a text box at the top or bottom of the page — a clean, empty chat window opens. If you don't see "New chat," look for a **pencil icon**, a **plus sign (+)**, or simply click into the existing chat box to start a fresh message. You'll know it worked when you see a blank message field with a blinking cursor and a "Send" or arrow button nearby.

## Step 2 — Tell Cohere what your project is
Click into the message field and write one or two sentences describing your project in plain words. The more specific you are about the vibe you want (fun, serious, modern, cozy, weird), the closer the names will land. After you press send, Cohere will acknowledge your message — usually with a short reply like "Got it" or a direct attempt at your request. If nothing appears for a few seconds, wait a moment, then check that your message actually went through (look for your text in the chat history).
💬 Example: "I'm starting a weekend walking club in my neighborhood. I want names that feel friendly, casual, and a little playful — nothing too formal."
You'll know it worked when Cohere responds to your setup message instead of the chat sitting empty.

## Step 3 — Ask for exactly 10 name ideas
Now send a follow-up message asking for a list of 10 names. Specifying the number helps — otherwise you may get 3 or 30. Cohere typically replies with a numbered or bulleted list. If your screen shows the reply as a wall of text, scroll down — the list is usually underneath. On mobile, the list may be cut off; just keep scrolling to see all 10.
💬 Example: "Great. Now please give me exactly 10 name ideas for this walking club. Mix practical names with a couple of quirky ones."
You'll know it worked when you can count (roughly) 10 distinct name suggestions in the reply.

## Step 4 — Push for more variety
Don't settle for the first round. Reply and ask for a different flavor — funnier, shorter, more professional, or inspired by a word you liked. Cohere will generate a fresh list based on your new direction. This is the step where the brainstorm really opens up, so don't be shy about steering.
💬 Example: "I like 'Sidewalk Stories' from your list. Can you give me 10 more names in that same warm, story-telling style?"
You'll know it worked when the new list feels noticeably different from the first one.

## Step 5 — Check availability and gut-feel
AI-generated names are creative, but they can sometimes be oddly generic, hard to spell, or already used by someone else. Read each name out loud. Type your top three into a search engine alongside words like "podcast," "shop," or "club" to see if anything similar already exists. What this tool **cannot** do is tell you whether a name is legally free to use or whether the domain is available — that's still on you. If a name feels close to a real brand you recognize, drop it.
You'll know it worked when you've narrowed your list to 2–3 favorites that sound good, are easy to say, and don't collide with anything you know.

## Step 6 — Save your favorites somewhere real
Copy the names you like into a note on your phone, a sticky note, or a simple document. Don't just trust that you'll remember them tomorrow — you won't. If Cohere's interface offers a way to copy the whole chat (sometimes a small "copy" icon near each reply), use it. If not, highlight the names with your finger or mouse and copy them by hand.
You'll know it worked when you can close the browser, open your notes, and see your shortlist waiting for you.

## Common mistakes
- **Asking for "a good name" with no context.** The AI has nothing to work with, so you'll get bland, generic suggestions like "Project One." Always include what the project is and the mood you want.
- **Accepting the first list without pushing back.** The first round is just a starting point. If the names feel off, tell the AI what to change ("make them shorter," "add something nature-themed") and ask again.
- **Forgetting to check if a name already exists.** AI can accidentally invent a name that's already a well-known brand, podcast, or trademark. A quick search saves you a future headache.

## What this means for you
- **In everyday life:** Naming a baby? A new email address? A group-chat for the family? The same prompt style works for anything you need a short, memorable label for.
- **For your business or work:** You can use the same trick for product feature names, internal project codenames, blog series titles, or workshop names. Just swap the context in your prompt.
- **If you're just getting started:** Try it once on something small and low-stakes — like naming your photo folder for a vacation. The more you practice writing clear prompts, the better your results will be on bigger projects.

## Try it now
Open Cohere, type: *"Give me 10 name ideas for a casual Sunday-morning podcast about cooking breakfast with whatever's in the fridge. Keep the names short and fun."* See what comes back. Your favorite is probably hiding in that list.
